question: The windows a player makes and manages convoys with: convoy_creation_window, convoy_details, convoy_settings, the production screen's convoy_queue rows and convoy_button, and the commands they post.

addresses.name: CConvoyProvinceEntry::OnClick
addresses.comment: Slot 4: a click on a port's row: the creation window's chosen province (+0x30) = this row's province (+0x28) and its `picked` byte (+0x3C) = 1. Nothing else - the window acts on it from its slot 8 the next frame. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Six instructions: `mov eax,[ecx+0x28]; mov ecx,[ecx+0x2C]; mov byte [ecx+0x3C],1; mov [ecx+0x30],eax; ret` (decompiled and listed). Slot 4 of the vftable at VA 0x15DDD74.

Stores settings (+0x34) and the view (+0x38); supplies byte (+0x28) 0, picking-origin (+0x29) 1, origin and chosen 0, picked 0; attaches `cancel`; fills the list once. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CConvoyCreationWindow::Open
addresses.comment: **`create_supply` (1) or `create_resource` (0)**: +0x28 = supplies, +0x29 = 1 (the first choice is the origin), +0x2C = 0, +0x3C = 0; `title` = CDW_ORIGIN ("Select Port of Origin for Convoy"); the list filled (CConvoyCreationWindow::FillList); the window shown and brought up (its slot 13 and slot 11). `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0x7DFE30-0x7E001F; the two callers 0x7E3860/0x7E3870 are `mov eax,[ecx+0x44]; push 1 (or 0); push eax; call`. Would be wrong if 0x7E3860 were attached to create_resource and not create_supply: CConvoySettings::Bind (0x7E2D80) attaches create_supply to the glue at +0x74 whose handler the constructor sets to 0x7E3860.

addresses.name: CConvoyCreationWindow::OnCancel
addresses.comment: The creation window's `cancel` button: hides the window (the settings' creation window's secondary table at +0x1C, slot 12). No command. **The button is drawn at x=5770 in both installs' files, off every screen (`##todo:remove`), so the mouse cannot reach it.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Five instructions at 0x7E0030 (tail call through +0x34 -> +0x44 -> +0x1C -> slot 0x30). Position 5770,580 read from interface/convoys.gui and tfh/interface/convoys.gui.

addresses.name: CConvoyCreationWindow::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 8, called each frame from CConvoySettings::Update. Nothing until a row was clicked (+0x3C). If it was the origin choice (+0x29 set): +0x29 = 0, +0x2C = +0x30, `title` = CDW_DESTINATION ("Select Destination Port for Convoy"), the list filled again. If it was the destination: a CCreateConvoyCommand(+0x2C's id, +0x30's id, +0x28) posted to the session channel and the window hidden. +0x3C = 0 either way. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read on the listing 0x7E0050..0x7E02A2; `call 0x549EA0` at 0x7E00B8 is the only constructor call site of CCreateConvoyCommand in the image (findRefs).

addresses.name: CConvoyCreationWindow::FillList
addresses.comment: **Which ports the convoy creation window offers.** Clears `list`, then for each of the player's controlled provinces (CCountry +0xD00, in list order) with owner id not 0, a port (+0x354) and a naval base of level_max above 0 (+0x300 -> +0x20), and which is not already the origin (+0x2C): capital-area = province.area (+0x2B4) == acting capital's area. `capitalAreaWanted` = (+0x28 supply convoy == +0x29 picking origin). **Supply convoy**: origin must be in the capital's area; destination must not be, unless supply_depot_hops (+0x50) > SUPPLY_SAME_AREA_DIST_CUTOFF/1000 (10 in Their Finest Hour); and either way refused where any non-trade, non-lend-lease convoy carrying supplies or fuel already ends at the province. **Resource convoy**: origin must not be in the capital's area and its area must have no convoy starting in it (COwnerArea +0x4..+0x8 empty); destination must be in the capital's area. Each passing province gets a CConvoyProvinceEntry, appended with listbox slot 4 (+0x10)(entry, 1). `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoywindows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0x7E02B0-0x7E05E6, three callers (0x7DFD82, 0x7DFFEF, 0x7E028C). The branch logic is the listing's, and the define is read from military block +0x40 and matches its name's place in defines.lua (SUPPLY_SAME_AREA_DIST_CUTOFF = 10, both installs). Would be wrong if the +0x28 byte meant the opposite: Open sets it from the (button, argument) pair above and CCreateConvoyCommand's `supply` is that byte.
